items.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: And Jimmy Giuffre. That was the band, and Shorty, it was a quintet.

ctx.x: That’s probably a lot more than some people were making though, huh?

Well to me it was great you know. Of course what was great was playing with these guys, playing with Shelly and that kind of a rhythm section, Curtis Counce was in the rhythm section, Curtis played bass. And Jimmy Giuffre. That was the band, and Shorty, it was a quintet. And it was a long tour. It started in San Diego and we might have even played in Syracuse, I don’t — it was called The Festival of Modern American Jazz, 195 — end of ’54. And it was Stan Kenton’s orchestra, Art Tatum trio, Charlie Ventura with…

items.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Jimmy Guiffre came over too for that... And I hadn’t seen Guif in a long time.

ctx.x: “At a performance in Tokyo’s Buddakan Stadium the group drew over 100,000 enthusiastic fans.” This was the Lighthouse All-Stars. Wow. Japan loves jazz, don’t they?

Wonderful. Yeah it was a wonderful trip, it was just a great trip. Shelly was on that trip and Shorty of course, Bud Shank, Jimmy Guiffre came over too for that, flew in from Massachusetts. And I hadn’t seen Guif in a long time.
